thread:
nina: Manager question  we had a promo approved but paperwork missed the payroll cutoff. Candidate's change effective date was 2026-06-01. What's the standard process for appeals / urgent backpay?

omar: short: default is retro pay processed in next 1-2 payroll cycles after approval. Appeals can request expedited processing but need a documented packet.

kevin_hr: to be concrete, the appeals packet should include: manager justification, signed evidence, director ack, comp partner sign-off, and a short note on business impact. Without complete docs payroll won't expedite.

nina: manager wants to ask for an exception citing candidate retention risk. What counts as acceptable "business impact" evidence?

comp-team: examples that help: written counteroffers from other companies, exec sponsor email requesting exception, revenue/customer-impact note (1-2 lines). We need something tangible; "we're worried" alone is weak.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: Promo Appeals policy v1.0 requires Appeals packets to be submitted within 30 days of effective date and routed to Comp Committee for exceptions. See: https://redwoodintra/confluence/promotions/appeals

kevin_hr: timeline: if manager files an appeal within 30 days and includes exec sponsor approval, people-ops will route to Comp Committee for an expedited review window of 5 business days. Payroll can attempt an out-of-cycle retro within that window if Comp Committee approves.

omar: operational note: payroll needs signed forms and final Workday entry before they can push an out-of-cycle retro. So even with committee approval, the manager must complete the Workday case immediately.

nina: ok. Is there a template managers should use for the appeal packet? saves back-and-forth.

people-ops-bot: Action: /task create "Promo Appeals packet template + email sample" assigned to kevin_hr, due 2026-05-05.

kevin_hr: I'll create a 1-page template (fields + checklist) and a 2-sentence email managers can send to exec sponsors.

comp-team: also add a required line: "Is this request linked to a recruitment/retention risk? yes/no + short evidence" so committee can triage.

omar: small practical: if comp committee denies exception, what's communicated to the employee? manager or people-ops sends a short note and offers next steps (delayed retro timeline, possible sign-on adjustment). We should standardize wording.

kevin_hr: agree. I'll draft two short templates: "approved" and "denied with next steps". Keep tone factual.

nina: one edge-case: what about multiple promos queued for the same payroll where one appeal is approved and others denied? payroll capacity could be a problem. Any guidance?

comp-team: capacity note: payroll may bundle retro batches weekly. If multiple appeals approved, payroll will schedule them in the next doable batch; timeline communicated by payroll. We should tell managers to expect up to 2 cycles in high volume months.

people-ops-bot: FYI attached schedules: https://redwoodintra/drive/payroll/cutovers-2026.xlsx.

nina: last ask  can we get a 2-line manager-facing FAQ I can paste in the hiring thread?

kevin_hr: draft: "If a promotion misses the payroll cutoff, retro pay is typically processed within 1-2 cycles after approvals. To request an exception for expedited retro, submit an Appeals packet (manager justification, director and comp approvals, evidence of business impact) within 30 days; Comp Committee will target a 5-business-day expedited review when an exec sponsor is included."

nina: perfect, thanks. Closing thread once kevin posts the template. :white_check_mark:
